Dona Maria Wines.zin: Dona Maria Wines The classy range of wines produced by Júlio Bastos betrays his roots.

Falésia.zin: The once heavily planted coastal strip is typified by sand or mixed sand and clay, but it was Falésia’s propitious clifftop calcareous/black volcanic soil that encouraged Iain and Feann Brown to plant vines at Quinta dos Castanhos.

Fita Preta.zin: Fita Preta Co-founded in 2004 by winemaker António Maçanita and David Booth, the late viticulturist after whom the flagship red is named.

In the rugged uplands, Ana Matias Chaves’ ‘little schist mountain’ at Herdade Barranco do Vale produces firmly structured whites and reds.

Herdade do Mouchão.zin: Herdade do Mouchão introduced Alentejo to its most structured variety, Alicante Bouschet and, for over a century, it has been foot-trodden and whole-bunch fermented in lagares, then aged in old 5,000-litre Portuguese oak barrels (tonels).

Herdade do Rocim.zin: Herdade do Rocim not only has two talha cellars (one ancestral and one modern) but now organises the annual Amphora Wine Day, where producers from all over Portugal, and beyond, show their amphora-fermented and aged wines.
South Portugal: Alentejo Catarina Vieira & Pedro Ribeiro Herdade do Rocim Arriving with a bang, Herdade do Rocim was founded in 2000 by entrepreneur José Ribeiro Vieira of Movicortes Group.

Howards Folly.zin: Thus far Howards Folly have released a 1991 and 1995 Colheita, in each case back-blending a splash of wine from the following year.

José Maria da Fonseca.zin: José Maria da Fonseca Owned by the Soares Franco family since the 1820s, José Maria da Fonseca is Portugal’s oldest, most venerable producer of Moscatel de Setúbal, Portugal’s other world-class fortified wine.

João Portugal Ramos.zin: ‘Private winemakers and wine-growers brought quality and innovation to the region,’ explains João Portugal Ramos, then one of a cohort of highly sought-after young Portuguese consultant winemakers, whose number included Paulo Laureano, Rui Reguinga and Luis Duarte.

Mouchão.zin: Herdade do Mouchão Acquired by John Reynolds in 1874, whose descendants pioneered Alicante Bouschet and still make it traditionally, using century-old stone lagares, basket presses and 5,000-litre tonéis.

Quinta da Corrieira.zin: In 2021, the region was extended to northern Oeiras to include Quinta da Corrieira, paving the way for the 2024 launch of Quinta da Corrieira Colheita 2012, the first Carcavelos wine in more than 20 years to have been produced by a private estate, such is its rarity.

Quinta da Fonte Souto.zin: Compared with those I tasted from Altas Quintas a decade ago, Quinta da Fonte Souto reds are especially much more sophisticated.

As for retail, Tanners Wine Merchants has already placed a second order for Quinta do Francês, whose range Emma Pook (author of Tanners Wines Blog) discovered on a family holiday last year.

Quinta do Mouro.zin: Grown at 400m elevation on lean, schist soils, Quinta do Mouro and, especially Quinta do Mouro Rótulo Dourado (‘Gold Label’, launched in 2000), are well-structured, long-lived and complex.

Ramilo.zin: Departing from tradition (hence the Lisboa Vinho Regional classification), Ramilo’s pioneering rosé is vinified from 300kg of its 2,000kg haul of the rare red Ramisco grape.

Domaine Robert Groffier.zin: Quantities in Chambolle were as generous as elsewhere – there was enough fruit for Nicolas Groffier of Domaine Robert Groffier to offer multiple cuvées of both grand cru Bonnes-Mares and premier cru Les Amoureuses.

Domaine Séguinot-Bordet.zin: The Chablis ‘Vieilles Vignes’ from Domaine Séguinot-Bordet comes in at just over £20 and offers a great deal of fruit purity and an energy on the palate which makes one want to drink another glass.

Domaine Trapet Père et Fils.zin: Louis Trapet at Domaine Trapet Père et Fils agrees about yield: ‘2023 is the maximum; 2024 is the minimum.’ Acid management They started to pick on 6 September and ended on the 18 with the Côte de Beaune, harvesting the grands crus just before the rain on 12 September.

Domaine William Fèvre.zin: Didier Séguier from Domaine William Fèvre, which also has vines in Les Clos, says: ‘Normally we employ 160 pickers for 9-10 days of picking.
The wines of Domaine William Fèvre are stunning across the board.

Domaine de Montille.zin: Brian Sieve, chef de cave at Domaine de Montille, said Pommard needed a ripe year to shine, and that ripening was aided by the dryness of the year, adding that it was one of the five driest vintages ever.
Brian Sieve, winemaker at Domaine de Montille, says that much of the vineyard work was done earlier to preserve freshness in the wine and combat the effects of global warming.

Domaine de la Commaraine.zin: Domaine de la Commaraine, Pommard Although I have been following the wines for several years, I tasted for the first time at the Château de la Commaraine with technical director Paul Krug at the estate itself in autumn 2025.

Domaine de la Romanée-Conti.zin: Nonetheless, the unsurprising top-scorer was from Domaine de la Romanée-Conti, with the domaine’s La Tâche 2022 getting the seal of approval from Charles Curtis MW during his in-bottle tasting this spring.

Domaine de la Romanée-Conti first produced a red Corton in 2009 from 2.27 hectares that they lease from the heirs of the Domaine Prince Florent de Merode (in Corton Bressandes, Clos du Roi, and Renardes).

Domaine des Comtes Lafon.zin: If money is no object, invest in the Montrachet from Domaine des Comtes Lafon or the Chevalier-Montrachet from Domaine Jean Chartron or Domaine Michel Niellon.
Pierre Lafon of Domaine des Comtes Lafon says: ‘2024 was really hard in the vineyard but really easy in the cellar’.

Domaine des Lambrays.zin: At Domaine des Lambrays they made no changes, and winemaker Jacques Devauges describes his process: ‘We sorted like madmen, with three sorting tables, but we didn’t change the proportions of whole bunches: 40% for the premiers crus and 80% for the Clos des Lambrays.

Domaine du Comte Liger-Belair.zin: At Domaine du Comte Liger-Belair, Louis-Michel Liger-Belair was forthright about the struggles, reporting picking his Clos du Château later than he might have, and having to leave 30%-40% of the grapes from his new vineyard La Croix Rameau on the sorting table because of mildew.

Georges Duboeuf.zin: All 13 bottles supplied by Beaujolais giant Georges Duboeuf scored well across different Crus and quality tiers, while Korean-born, US-educated and French-trained newcomer Mee Godard was a hit with every wine: a young producer well worth following.

Guy Breton.zin: Domaine Guy Breton At just under 7ha, Domaine Guy Breton is modest in size but not reputation.

Jean-Paul Brun.zin: Jean-Paul Brun is a leading producer of white wine in the Beaujolais region, and claims that the limestone soils in the south are the reason for Chardonnay’s success.

Joseph Drouhin.zin: According to Frédéric Drouhin, CEO of Maison Joseph Drouhin, ‘2024 is a vintage of delicacy, sobriety and precision.

Julien Sunier.zin: Julien Sunier, a newcomer to the Beaujolais region in 2003, says this new generation are putting their energy into organics, respecting the environment and vinifying their own wines, as opposed to selling in bulk.

Louis Jadot.zin: Louis Jadot makes both under the name Clos de la Croix de Pierre, rather than the vineyard name; however, since the Chardonnay stretches from the premier cru band to a portion classified as village-level, it isn’t a premier cru.

Louis Latour.zin: The main, and unexpected, exception was Louis Latour, whose Chaumes premier cru as well as the top-scoring Petits Monts showed well.

Maison Champy.zin: Maison Champy, Chambolle-Musigny 2014 It was a very pleasant surprise to discover this was a Champy wine as it’s been a while since their wines have excited me.

Maison Chanzy.zin: Best producers: Clos de Cellier aux Moines Domaine du Meix Foulot Domaine Belleville Maison Chanzy Domaine Génot-Boulanger Mâconnais Yields in the Mâconnais were more moderate than elsewhere.

Michel Bouzereau.zin: Pierre Lafon explains: ‘Even if July and [early] August were cool, the struggle today is to maintain acidity.’ Michel Bouzereau describes a year that began ahead of schedule in May and June but fell behind with a period of cold and rain from mid-July.

Patrick Piuze.zin: Patrick Piuze picked 2014 and 2015, Vincent Dauvissat chose 2014 and 2002, and Benoît Droin nominated 2014 and 2010.

Pierre-Yves Colin-Morey.zin: Chassagne producer Domaine Pierre-Yves Colin-Morey was not far behind.

Rijckaert.zin: Winemaker Florent Rouve of Vins Rijckaert notes that excessively hot and dry conditions caused vines to shut down in August, which helped keep alcohol levels in check.

Samuel Billaud.zin: A tasting of Samuel Billaud’s range showed why he is now considered another Chablis superstar.

Simonnet-Febvre.zin: Further to the southwest of Chablis, Simonnet-Febvre is now setting out to reinvigorate the vineyards of the lesser-known IGP Coteaux de l’Auxois.

Adelaida.zin: And as it happens, California’s oldest Pinot Noir plantings south of Sonoma County are in what is now the Adelaida District, in the hills on Paso’s west side: the 59-year-old HMR Vineyard, owned by the Van Steenwyk family’s Adelaida Vineyards & Winery.

I was running back and forth like a chicken out there.’ The Adelaida team are the third guardians of HMR now, but its Pinot Noir and Chardonnay are part of California’s vinous heritage still flying under the radar.

Alta Colina.zin: Molly Lonborg at Alta Colina said: ‘Because of our high elevation, we have a lot of high-intensity fruit, a lot of colour and a lot of tannin.’ Soils are limestone dominant with water-retaining properties and give the ability to retain freshness and acidity in the wines.

Booker.zin: Similarly, back at Booker, Graves says: ‘The more we have focused on soil health, the more resilient our vines have become.’ Booker’s 35ha Willow Creek District estate vineyard is certified organic and Regenerative Organic Certified (ROC).

Epoch Estate.zin: Jordan Fiorentini of Epoch Estate calls 2021 ‘a winemaker’s vintage where we could wait to pick the fruit until we felt it was time, without too many climatic factors getting in the way’.

Giornata.zin: Thacher, Giornata and Torrin are all husband-and-wife teams bringing up the next generation of Paso people and making wines that speak to both their origin and their audience.

Saxum Vineyards.zin: ‘The wines are tasty and the tannins are soft,’ says Justin Smith, owner and winemaker at Saxum Vineyards, ‘similar to 2017, the most recent hot vintage.’ The wines can broadly be described as approachable and open-knit.

Tablas Creek.zin: At Tablas Creek’s Adelaida estate vineyard, December was the wettest month on record, receiving 350mm of rain out of the annual total of 500mm.
The Haas and Perrin family partnership of Tablas Creek is a good example of personal and practical ambition.

Thacher.zin: The choice of rootstocks or own-rooted as per Thacher’s Shell Creek Vineyard Chenin Blanc, row spacing, clonal selection, irrigation techniques and the ability to dry-farm, are just a few of the ongoing areas of research and trial.
Thacher is one of many in family-run wineries in Paso Robles.

Littorai.zin: Ted Lemon of Littorai called it a ‘head-scratcher’ one that, in the end, has produced brilliant, beautiful wines from the Sonoma Coast.

Williams Selyem.zin: In addition, names like Cobb, Peay and Williams Selyem have long been spreading the word about what this region can achieve.

Aroma Winery.zin: Aroma Winery, owned by Raffaele Noviello, has been able to make its way in increasingly competitive markets.’ Born in Irpinia in 1980, Noviello founded Mont’Antico winery at the age of 24, renaming it Aroma Winery in 2014.

Nk’Mip.zin: ‘It snowed right after the last pick of Cab Sauvignon on 7 November.’ Late harvest In Osoyoos, Justin Hall at Nk’Mip had to machine-pick Syrah in -2°C temperatures to get it off before snow on 3 November.

Peak Cellars.zin: O’Rourke Peak Cellars and Culmina’s Grüner Veltliners come from opposite ends of the valley but are equally compelling.

Synchromesh.zin: The Loire-esque Synchromesh and joyfully juicy Ursa Major were immediate standouts.

Tantalus.zin: From the Kelowna area, Tantalus Old Vines and Martin’s Lane Fritzi’s Vineyard are two of my top drops of the entire vintage.

Charles Heidsieck.zin: This was one of the rare vintages of the revived Charles Heidsieck Champagne Charlie cuvée, which I was lucky enough to taste when I visited Charles Heidsieck.

Laurent-Perrier.zin: Laurent-Perrier’s Alexandra rosé is the perfect example of this; an icon of its style.

Louis Roederer.zin: ‘You can plant more Chardonnay, but you can’t plant more Côte des Blancs!’ says Louis Roederer’s chef de cave Jean-Baptiste Lécaillon, a believer in the ‘freshness’ that the chalk soils, with their unique water-retentive properties, bestow on the wines.

Pierre Péters.zin: Pierre Péters’ Les Chétillons Grand Cru 2009 was cream of the crop.

Pol Roger.zin: ‘Whether he had money or not, Churchill continued buying Pol Roger throughout his life,’ he adds, hinting that Churchill may have consumed – or at least ordered – as many as 42,000 bottles.
Pol Roger’s production methods may have changed since Churchill’s days, but the house continues to make its Cuvée Sir Winston Churchill in the Churchillian spirit.

Baettig.zin: Benchmark Cab: the names to know and wines to seek out Chile Baettig With his enviable flair for elegant Cabernet, Francisco Baettig has been reviving the overlooked region of Maule with a beautiful duo of Cabernet Sauvignons from his eponymous label.

Carmen.zin: They don’t come bigger in Chile than Concha y Toro but, tasting the Marqués de Casa Concha Cabernet Sauvignon 2018 or the Terrunyo Carmenère 2018 is like discovering a new world of elegance and precision, where before the accent was on power and heft.

From an altogether more establishment player, Carmen’s Florillón Semillon is also an impressive wine aged under a yeast veil ‘that does liposuction on the wine’, according to its maker Emily Faulconer, meaning it is ‘leaner and sharper’.

Clos Santa Ana.zin: Clos Santa Ana Luiz Allegretti and Roberto Ibarra’s young organic project is already producing stunning wines.

Concha y Toro.zin: Concha y Toro, Don Melchor Now celebrating its 35th vintage, Don Melchor is a well-established icon of Chile.

Cono Sur.zin: Cono Sur Cono Sur is based in Colchagua, but Silencio, one of the top wines in the portfolio, comes from prime plots a little further north in Maipo Andes.

Estampa.zin: The best examples are from Estampa, Koyle (Costa Cuarzo Sauvignon Blanc) and Casa Silva (Cool Coast Sauvignon Blanc).

La Ronciere.zin: A standout project in this regard is La Ronciere’s Idahue Estate in Licantén.

Miguel Torres Chile.zin: Miguel Torres Chile, Manso de Velasco One of the most prized vineyards that Spanish winemaking pioneer Miguel Torres discovered when establishing his Chilean outpost from 1979 (the vineyard was purchased in 1984).

Montes.zin: ‘We’d had a similar experience with our Sauvignon Blanc, so we had our concerns,’ remembers Aurelio Montes, then a consultant to Fundación Chile (the think tank that had brought ampelographer Boursiquot to Chile) and now one of Chile’s most prominent Carmenère champions.
However, there are areas far away with no river access.’ Montes has reduced water consumption by 65% on its Apalta estate by switching to sustainable dry-farming.

San Pedro.zin: The Altair brand has been fully owned by San Pedro since 2007, when Château Dassault abandoned the partnership, though with Chatonnet and Cumsille retained on the winemaking team.
Until then, San Pedro had focused on more marketable brands – not least the popular Gato Negro label – with all production based at the historical winery in Molina.

Santa Carolina.zin: Other major names, including Santa Carolina, Concha y Toro and Casa Silva, are also advocates of this school.

Santa Rita.zin: Alto Jahuel is part of Chile’s vinous patrimony and it is the main artery for Santa Rita’s 100 million-litre production – including its Carmen brand and Casa Real, one of Chile’s foremost icon wines.
‘We have learned that you can push the limits with Carmenère,’ says Santa Rita winemaker Sebastián Labbé, who started experimenting with a radically fresher style of Carmenère in 2017.

Undurraga.zin: The TH line-up is a comparatively small part of what Urrejola does – Undurraga is among the biggest wineries in Chile – but it’s the one that has propelled him to the front rank of the country’s winemakers since it began in 2011.

‘The old vines naturally produce very small bunches, which mature really well,’ explains Undurraga winemaker Rafael Urrejola, whose Extinto vineyard in Cachapoal, south of Santiago, is more than 75 years old.

Viu Manent.zin: Viu Manent Under head winemaker Patricio Celedón, Viu Manent has pushed towards lighter styles over the past five years, picking earlier and using older foudres and less new oak.

Viña Quebrada de Macul.zin: Viña Quebrada de Macul A cult Cabernet Sauvignon producer in Chile, this boutique winery is one of the better-kept secrets of Macul.

Casa Marín.zin: Casa Marín is the only producer here; its founder, María Luz Marín, Chile’s first female winemaker, planted her vineyard just 4km from the Pacific, against the advice of other wine professionals but with a firm belief in the potential of cool-climate wines in Chile.

Viña Leyda.zin: Viña Leyda was a pioneer in Leyda, planting vines in 1998, releasing its first wine in 2001 and successfully petitioning for the creation of the Leyda Valley DO in 2002.

Viña Marty.zin: Viña Marty, meanwhile, is using sake yeast to enable cool ferments and longer lees ageing, for extra structure.

A Los Viñateros Bravos.zin: The A Los Viñateros Bravos’ Granítico and Pipeño labels (see tasting notes, p54) equate to ‘village’ wines, from soils with a higher proportion of clay.

De Martino.zin: He started working at De Martino in 1996 and has transformed the style of the winery’s reds and whites, moving them towards lower alcohol, less extraction and little or no oak.

Leonardo Erazo.zin: The Leonardo Erazo ‘premier crus’ (such as Las Curvas, La Ruptura, Hombre en Llamas and El Tunel) come from soils where rock predominates over clay; and for the Leonardo Erazo ‘grand cru’ Amigo Piedra, the soils are rockier still.
Wines under the Leonardo Erazo label (featuring a drawing of an owl on the label) are sourced from parcels that Erazo owns or manages himself, some no bigger than a few rows.

Rogue Vine.zin: Altos is focused on Malbec, especially Malbec grown on limestone soils, whereas Rogue Vine and Leonardo Erazo specialise in blended reds and whites from grapes such as Cinsault and País, Muscat and Semillon, grown on unirrigated granitic soils.

Clos Alivu.zin: She produces Clos Teddi, his vines furnish Clos Alivu, and I find it hard to choose between their mouthwatering Vermentinos and polished, spicy reds.

Maestracci.zin: Camille-Anaïs Raoust of Maestracci told me she only invested in temperature control over the past couple of years, as her recently retired father was reluctant to spend the money.

Aliança.zin: Bairrada: 10 names to know Aliança As its extensive underground cellars attest, the Bairrada outpost of one of Portugal’s biggest producers, Bacalhôa Vinhos, was itself a leviathan during the heyday of bulk exports to Africa and Brazil.

Buçaco.zin: Retaining a foot in the négociant camp, Buçaco Reservado is made from Buçaco’s and growers’ grapes in Buçaco Palace Hotel’s cellars.

Casa de Mouraz.zin: When it comes to replanting reds, Casa de Mouraz’s Sara Dionísio contends: ‘You can’t be only focused on Touriga Nacional, or we’ll lose the diversity.’ There are other perfumed, lighter-bodied, fresh varieties, which align perfectly with Dão’s classic profile.
Casa de Mouraz Launched in 2000, Lisboetas António Lopes Ribeiro and Sara Dionísio left the arts to make wine from Ribeiro’s family’s certified-organic, aged field blend vineyards in Besteiros.

Caves São João.zin: During the négociant era, bulk wine for colonies was the principal focus, however the Costa brothers of Caves São João famously bottled the cream of the Dão crop under the Porta dos Cavaleiro brand, Reserva Seleccionada being the finest.

Global Wines.zin: Global Wines A multi-regional producer, but Dão, where it owns/manages 300ha, is a region of origin and focus.

João Tavares de Pina.zin: Playful, ‘glou-glou’ (gluggable) and natural wines have also emerged, of which João Tavares de Pina is the master, using chestnut flowers as an antioxidant and antibacterial, plus – being a committed locovore – large Portuguese chestnut barrels too.

Luis Pato.zin: Producers to look for: Campolargo Filipa Pato & William Wouters Luis Pato Luis Patrão Fonte Cal White; total area planted: 50ha The word ‘cal’ means ‘limestone’ in Portuguese and this grape is associated with the limestone-rich area of Pinhel in Beira Interior.

Niepoort.zin: Quinta de Baixo Acquired by Niepoort in 2012, the Cantanhede-based estate is cultivated biodynamically.

Quinta das Bágeiras.zin: Quinta das Bágeiras Stellar, fuller-bodied white, red and zero dosage sparkling range; the whole-bunch fermented Bagas are brooding and dark-fruited.

Quinta do Perdigão.zin: Quinta do Perdigão With its olive grove, wild flowers, honeybees and roaming horse, the bucolic, walled 7ha estate in Silgueiros, owned by architect and artist José and Vanessa Perdigão, is among the prettiest.

Quinta dos Roques.zin: Quinta dos Roques An extremely consistent third-generation Terras de Azurara estate (as is its certified-organic Serra da Estrela sister label, Quinta das Maias).

Burmester.zin: Carlos Alves, winemaker for Barros, Burmester, Cálem and Kopke, echoes Symington when he says: ‘We had to make profound use of the knowledge of our grapes, as each variety and each plot of vineyard developed at a different pace.

Casa Ferreirinha.zin: However, named after the diminutive lady (‘little Ferreira’), Casa Ferreirinha Barca Velha was originally – and for many years – made and principally sourced from Meão.
From the ‘stars-aligned’ 2011 Douro vintage, Casa Ferreirinha Barca Velha – the original icon – is a shoo-in.

Ferreira.zin: Luís Sottomayor from Ferreira and Sandeman describes 2019 as ‘a very good year with freshness and great balance’.
Luís Sottomayor, responsible for Ferreira, Offley and Sandeman is even more fulsome.

Folias de Baco.zin: Tiago Sampaio (Folias de Baco) has planted Pinot Noir and Tinta Francisca there for single-varietal wines, while his Uivo Renegado – a sappy 50/50, white/red old field-blend wine – reflects a niche revival of lighter-bodied ‘palhete’ or ‘clarete’ wines.

Fonseca.zin: Going back to the 1980s, there is a caveat emptor on some of the 1985s, though Fonseca is faultless and in my opinion the leading wine of the vintage.
From 1977, Fonseca is a tower of strength with Dow’s and Graham’s 1970 both worthy of being ranked alongside the 20th-century greats.

Graham's.zin: Graham's Quinta dos Malvedos is the source of its The Stone Terraces Port: 'the quintessence of the finest Douro fruit' according to Richard Mayson in his report.

Luis Seabra.zin: Take Luis Seabra’s wines, which showcase whole-bunch ferments – another tool increasingly used to create a sense of freshness and levity, not least because, says Seabra, ‘it forces me not to extract too much’.

Niepoort.zin: Niepoort says Paulson’s bottle of La Tâche 1991 prompted him to ask: ‘How is it possible that the wine is so aromatic, yet so fine?’ Picked early, Charme is fermented with 100% stems to ‘fool everyone and make the wine look like it has more acidity than it actually does’.

‘Tannin is something that is not lacking in most Douro varieties’ Francisco Olazabal A pendulum swing Chief among them is Niepoort, whose quest for freshness has seen him push the envelope hardest on earlier picking and big-format oak (foudres and vats).

Portugal Boutique Winery.zin: Portugal Boutique Winery’s lighter-styled Boina Red highlighted the benefits of aged (centenarian) vines, using fast-disappearing varieties such as Gouveio-Preto, Tinta Carvalha, Alicante Bouschet and Alvarelhão.

Prats & Symington.zin: Though similarly focused on the Tourigas (with a splash of Tinta Amarela), the Prats & Symington wines made for an interesting comparison with SFE’s Douro wines from Quinta do Vesuvio, one of Chryseia’s original sources.

Quinta Nova.zin: Quinta Nova’s trio of 92-pointers also showed an impressive and nuanced grip of the market.

Quinta de la Rosa.zin: Some of the properties below (such as Quinta do Noval, Quinta de la Rosa and Quinta do Vesúvio) have become shippers in their own right, producing a range of wines (both Port and Douro) as well as a Single Quinta Vintage Port nearly every year.

Quinta do Crasto.zin: Quinta do Crasto’s Maria Teresa comes from a plot of 54 grape varieties from heritage vines, according to Miguel Roquette, who says ‘the recipe is in the field’.
There has also been an increase in Douro wines – a category pioneered by Quinta do Crasto, who first produced Vinha Maria Teresa and Vinha da Ponte in 1998.

Quinta do Noval.zin: We don’t have a back library of vintages to show the ageing potential yet – but we will.’ Quinta do Noval wines: new releases You might also like: Quinta do Noval declares 2019 Port vintage My Top 10: single quinta Ports Port vintage guide Explore More

That terroir surely accounts for Quinta do Noval ’s history of eccentric vintage declarations, starting with the Pinhão Valley quinta’s legendary 1931 vintage, and explains why it stands out in generally declared years, such as 2000.

Quinta do Vale Meão.zin: Claiming similarly distinguished roots, cousins Francisco Ferreira (Quinta do Vallado) and Francisco Olazábal (Quinta do Vale Meão) are descended from Dona Antónia Adelaide Ferreira who, respectively, owned and established their quintas during the 19th century.

At Quinta do Vale Meão, Francisco Olazabal points out, ‘tannin is something that is not lacking in most Douro varieties’, so his barrels are now ‘more neutral, with less toast, less wood sweetness and tannin’.

Quinta do Vallado.zin: Quinta do Vallado swiftly made its mark with mellifluous Tawny Ports with an indication of age (10, 20, 30 or 40-year-old) and impeccably sourced ultra-rare Very Old (19th century) Tawny Ports.

Ramos Pinto.zin: Ramos Pinto’s CEO Jorge Rosas is similarly taking ‘a closer zoom’ to showcase best performing parcels or blocks in top years with new Douro launch, Ramos Pinto Quinta de Ervamoira 2018.

Sandeman.zin: Graham’s, Late Bottled Vintage 2018 Sandeman, Late Bottled Vintage 2018 Tawny ‘Tawny’ covers a continuum of colours, styles and prices of Port from relatively young reserva, through 10, 20, 30, 40 and 50 years old.
Seixo is now the basis for Sandeman’s much-improved vintage Ports (the 2018 looks really very promising), but it has only been bottled quite rarely as a single quinta vintage.

Sogrape.zin: Antonini’s role directing Sogrape’s precision viticulture programme between 2008 and 2012 was immensely important, according to Guedes.

Titan of Douro.zin: From the Douro’s highest point, the granite and quartz slopes of Serra do Reboredo, Luís Leocádio (Titan of Douro) makes intensely characterful, mineral, fresh wines from un-grafted, 150-year-old vineyards planted at 700m-850m by his wife’s great grandfather.

Wine & Soul.zin: Since 2004, several elevated, old-vine parcels in Porrais have produced Wine & Soul Guru, an exceptional Douro white, recently joined by Guru NM, an innovative non-vintage iteration.
Wine & Soul’s riper, darker, muscular Pintas is from a sunnier, south-facing site in Vale de Mendiz which, observes Moreira, integrates oak more readily.

Bernhard Huber.zin: Julian Huber from the Bernhard Huber winery in Baden is also no slouch with his Schlossberg and Wildenstein from the Bienenberg.

Clemens Busch.zin: A handful of these late releases add some depth to the tasting notes below, and in fact Clemens Busch’s Marienburg Fahrlay-Terrassen Riesling Grosses Gewächs 2016 earns my joint-top mark.

Dönnhoff.zin: Robert Haller of Würzburg’s Bürgerspital reported that Silvaner was harvested even before Müller-Thurgau, while Anne Dönnhoff of the Dönnhoff estate in the Nahe reported that fruit was so wonderfully healthy that a ‘short, compact harvest’ was possible.
Style Dönnhoff is renowned for its racy, elegant wines which can have a potent mineral character and plenty of tension.

JJ Adeneuer.zin: Marc Adeneuer of JJ Adeneuer in the Ahr says of the 2016 Spätburgunders: ‘full ripeness, great acidity structure, ripe generosity but still mineral: I think it’s a grandiose vintage comparable to 2009.

Maximin Grünhaus.zin: Bruderberg The Bruderberg is named for the simple ‘brothers’ of the Maximin Grünhaus priory when the abbey was established more than a thousand years ago, as the wines from this parcel were designated for their consumption.
Dr Carl von Schubert of Maximin Grünhaus in the Ruwer said: ‘This year, Bruderberg was a magician.

Peter Jakob Kühn.zin: Peter Jakob Kühn, biodynamic pioneer of the Rheingau, says it all when he notes that his usual harvest team of 25 swelled to 40 in 2017.

Rudolf Fürst.zin: The wines from the Centgrafenberg and Hundsrück vineyards of the Rudolf Fürst winery are also among the finest Pinot Noirs: elegant and radiantly beautiful, with tannins so silky that they seem to be wearing a dinner jacket.

Wagner Stempel.zin: ‘Looking at pH was crucial in 2018,’ explained Daniel Wagner of Weingut Wagner Stempel in Rheinhessen, noting that he looked back at his records from 2003 to marvel how much he had learned since then.

Willi Schaefer.zin: In the face of global technological advances, the ethic at Weingut Willi Schaefer remains the same as it was in the days of Christoph’s grandfather and of those before him.
Weingut Willi Schaefer has 2ha of vines within this larger Grosse Lage cru.

Wittmann.zin: Philipp Wittmann of Weingut Wittmann in Rheinhessen said: ‘Indeed, a crazy year, but cool nights afforded us a vintage with German virtues: freshness, elegance and thankfully moderate alcohol levels, more classic than we all expected.

Zilliken.zin: Dorothee Zilliken of Weingut Forstmeister Geltz Zilliken in the Saar reported that, curiously, acid levels were lower than usual – still around the 7-8g/l mark, but with pH levels as low as ever at 2.9.

Ökonomierat Rebholz.zin: According to Hansjörg Rebholz, of Ökonomierat Rebholz in the Pfalz, ‘picking the right harvest point, not too early, not too late, was the biggest challenge of the year.’ But he also mused: ‘I think we have learned such a lot in the meantime when it comes to hot, dry years.

Karavitakis.zin: Another Nikos – Karavitakis – is convinced that Kotsifali, a grape traditionally used only in blends, has the potential to make outstanding varietal wines.

Monemvasia.zin: On the island of Paros, Monemvasia (white) and Mandilaria (red) are reasserting their traditional status, where they are co-fermented to produce supple, spicy red wines with some of the silkiness of wines such as Emmanuel Reynaud’s Château Rayas and Château des Tours.

Mylonas.zin: Producers like Papagiannakos, Akriotou and Mylonas in Attica have demonstrated its potential to make quality wines in a range of styles with character and ageing potential.
Stamatis Mylonas, an early believer whose Savatiano took home a DWWA Gold medal in 2014, is enthusiastic about the future.

Argillae.zin: With the Signorelli 500 label, Argillae is supporting the restoration of Orvieto cathedral, which is decorated with Renaissance frescoes by Luca Signorelli.

Cantina Terlano.zin: I have long been a fan of Cantina Terlano’s Vorberg Pinot Bianco, so to visit this revered site was something of a pilgrimage.

Le Due Terre.zin: Being an oenologist, she focuses on increasingly refined wines – a pure expression of the gifted terroir of origin, Prepotto.’ Le Due Terre owns 5ha of vineyards and has risen to prominence for its role in the re-evaluation of skin-macerated white wines.
‘Cora Basilicata is giving a decisive turning point to Le Due Terre winery, founded by her parents Flavio and Silvana.

Raúl Moreno.zin: I was blown away by Raúl Moreno ’s (pictured above) perfect encapsulations of technical precision and maverick questioning of stylistic assumptions.

Caveau de Bacchus.zin: Alice Aviet of Caveau de Bacchus says that the ‘extremes of temperature and rainfall are making it harder for organic producers to grow healthy grapes without treating their vines’.

Domaine André et Mireille Tissot.zin: Jura: six names to watch Domaine André et Mireille Tissot Stéphane Tissot is a leading player in the Jura.

Domaine Bourdy.zin: Domaine Bourdy has been making wines in the Jura for almost 450 years.

Domaine Jean-Louis Tissot.zin: Domaine Jean-Louis Tissot This is another branch of the Tissot family, with the estate run by Valérie and her brother Jean-Christophe on more traditional lines.

Domaine Pignier.zin: Domaine Pignier This domaine, run by Jean-Etienne, Antoine and Marie-Florence Pignier, has flown under the radar for an unseemly length of time.

Domaine de Montbourgeau.zin: A fine example of the former is the Domaine de Montbourgeau’s Cuvée Spéciale which is aged, like vin jaune, under a flor-like veil of yeast without topping up for four years.
Many topped-up whites, such as the elegant Chardonnays made by César Deriaux at Domaine de Montbourgeau in the village of L’Etoile, display subtly oxidative notes.

Domaine des Miroirs.zin: Domaine des Miroirs, perhaps the epitome of Jura’s cult wine phenomenon, was established by Kenjiro Kagami in Grusse, in Jura’s south, in time for a small first vintage in 2011.

François Rousset-Martin.zin: François Rousset-Martin who makes some of Jura’s finest expressions of Savagnin near the village of Château-Chalon, practises what he describes as ouillage à la jurassienne, topping up the maturing wine only about once a month.

Les Bottes Rouges.zin: Domaine Les Bottes Rouges A teacher-turned-winemaker, Jean-Baptiste Menigoz was mentored by Stéphane Tissot and named his 6ha property after a favourite song.

Les Granges Paquenesses.zin: Les Granges Paquenesses Loreline Laborde is representative of the new wave of growers in the Jura.

Marie-Pierre Chevassu-Fassenet.zin: Marie-Pierre Chevassu-Fassenet of the eponymous domaine in Menétrule-Vignoble describes how the ‘burning’ heat in 2022 went deep into even the marl, stressing young vines with shallow roots.

Calmel & Joseph.zin: This was the second tasting of this nature organised by négociant-producer Calmel & Joseph at the company domaine in Montirat, just outside Carcassonne.

Château Beauregard Mirouze.zin: Château Beauregard Mirouze, Corbières A domaine that’s newly on my radar, this is a young husband and wife team who have taken over the family estate, converting to organics in 2010 and biodynamics in 2018.

Château Coupe-Roses.zin: Sarah Frissant of Château Coupe-Roses in Minervois says they had only 250mm rainfall this growing season.

Château Maris.zin: Château Maris, Minervois A good example of making biodynamic wine at some scale, this domaine has made great leaps in pushing forward on sustainable viticulture and was one of the first European vineyards to obtain BCorp certification.

Château Ollieux Romanis.zin: Château Ollieux Romanis Now a sizeable 60ha domaine, Boutenacbased Château Ollieux Romanis is a reference in the region.

Château Rouquette sur Mer.zin: Languedoc latest releases homepage 2022 Vines at Château Rouquette sur Mer are less than 1km from the sea.

Château de Caraguilhes.zin: Adaptations and key trends Etienne Besancenot, director of Château de Caraguilhes in Boutenac, is forthright: ‘We must adapt viticulture and oenology to these climatic trends,’ he says.

Clos de l’Anhel.zin: ‘With Carignan, it’s all about yield,’ says Sophie Guiraudon of Clos de l’Anhel, where output turns around 25-30hl/ha.

Clos du Gravillas.zin: The Bojanowskis at Clos du Gravillas in St-Jean de Minervois are well-known supporters of ancient local varieties, with Terret, Clairette and Piquepoul thriving on their limestone soils in the region’s west.
New from Clos du Gravillas is I’m Alive, a carbonic maceration Vin de France blend of the ancient Piquepouls Blanc, Noir and Gris, with a touch of Cinsault.

Domaine Begude.zin: At Domaine Begude it ‘prompted the vines in to ripening correctly and we picked a few days after the downpour, ’ says Kinglake.
James Kinglake, owner of Domaine Begude, says the ‘frost at the end of April…decimated our lower, less windy vineyards ’.

Domaine Binet-Jacquet.zin: ‘Spring and summer were fresh and rainy, ’ says Pierre Jacquet of Domaine Binet-Jacquet, and in fact there was more rain over the summer than usual.

Domaine Danjou-Banessy.zin: ‘Old vines are like stubborn old men,’ says Benoît Danjou, co-owner of Domaine Danjou-Banessy in Espira-de-l’Agly, ‘they give what they want’ and can be difficult to manage.

Domaine La Linquière.zin: Domaine La Linquière A domaine of 25ha, it was the white that took my breath away here, Rolle and Grenache Blanc in a delicate blend of crushed rocks and apple blossom.

Domaine Le Champ des Murailles.zin: Owner Pierre Bories is also developing another estate at Fabrézan – Domaine Le Champ des Murailles – and its Grande Cuvée was a Gold medal winner at the 2018 Decanter World Wine Awards.

Domaine Ollier-Taillefer.zin: Domaine Ollier-Taillefer Run by brother and sister Luc and Françoise Ollier, this is an organic domaine of 36ha that offers excellent consistency in its range of wines.

Domaine de Baronarques.zin: The Domaine de Baronarques Grand Vin Rouge 2021 did have great depth of cassis fruit, but also some tight and drying tannins.

Domaine de Cébène.zin: Brigitte Chevalier of Domaine de Cébène admits that she wishes she had started using ceramic eggs and terracotta jars earlier than a few years ago, now saying: ‘I think that for the wines of Faugères, barrels are not justified.’ 5.
Domaine de Cébène Brigitte Chevalier has forged a path within this small Languedoc appellation and has become well known for producing wines of great finesse.

Domaine de La Cendrillon.zin: Elsewhere there has been heavy investment in estates such as the Domaines Barons de Rothschild Lafite-owned Domaine d’Aussières and Domaine de La Cendrillon, but it’s the smaller domaines that may eventually add impetus to Corbières’ renown in the Languedoc.
Domaine de La Cendrillon Sixth-generation owner Robert Joyeux has invested heavily in the 48ha property since taking over in 2011.

Domaine de Montcalmès.zin: Compare this to the price of Domaine de Montcalmès at €28, Mas Cal Demoura Les Cambariolles at €26 or Domaine d’Aupilhac Les Cocalières at €19 per bottle and there are bargains to be found.

Domaine de Petit Roubié.zin: Domaine de Petit Roubié An organic domaine with 80ha and a huge range of wines, many of which are single-variety IGP wines.

Domaine de Villeneuve.zin: Domaine de Villeneuve Run by Anne-Lisse Fraisse-Florac since 2005 who has now passed the reins to her 28-year-old daughter Victorine.
Victorine Fraisse, the new generation at Domaine de Villeneuve, says that the summer saw several storms, too.

Domaine de la Meunerie.zin: Some white Roussillon, such as Domaine de la Meunerie’s Argenta Brilo, are made of pure Grenache Gris.

Domaine des Deux Clés.zin: Domaine des Deux Clés This 14ha domaine in the Hautes- Corbières is a rising star.

Domaine du Grès Vaillant.zin: Sadly there aren’t many producers making 100% Mauzac still whites, but those from Domaine de Mouscaillo and Domaine du Grès Vaillant are particularly charming, with some of Mauzac’s typical apple profile but also a good grating of citrus zest and balancing acidity.
Domaine du Grès Vaillant A new project lead by the young Aigline de Causans and Laurent Maffeïs since 2017, Domaine du Grès Vaillant has eight hectares of vines among 70ha of woodland and meadow.

Domaine du Lendemain.zin: Domaine du Lendemain in Roussillon has some pre-phylloxera vines planted in 1880 that are still producing fruit.

Laurent Miquel.zin: Imported grapes On limestone above the village of Lagrasse in Corbières, Laurent Miquel has pioneered the planting of Albariño – the popular grape of Galicia in northwest Spain that Miquel had an inkling might work in Languedoc.

Le Chemin des Rêves.zin: Le Chemin des Rêves An ex-pharmacist who turned to winemaking, Benoît Viot is the current president of the appellation and now has 17ha of organic vines.

Le Clos du Serres.zin: Le Clos du Serres Also incomers to the region, Sébastien, who is also the appellation’s current president, and his wife Béatrice run this 15ha domaine and make elegant wines.

Les Clos Perdus.zin: Les Clos Perdus It was the old-vine Carignan and Mourvèdre that persuaded former professional dancer Paul Old to ditch plans to return to his native Australia.

Les Hautes Terres.zin: Geneviève and Gilles Azam of Les Hautes Terres, also in the Haute Vallée de l’Aude, say that 2021 is ‘elegant and discreet, ’ but stress that both 2021 and 2022 are both ‘very atypical vintages which really show how the climate is changing’.

Les Vignes Oubliées.zin: Les Vignes Oubliées A sort of small cooperative where the grapes come from a collective of a few farmers working tiny parcels as naturally as possible, and the wines are made by Jean-Baptiste Granier.

Mas Bruguière.zin: Mas Bruguière These wines are compelling; firm in their youth but refined.

Mas Conscience.zin: Mas Conscience A domaine which was relaunched in 2020 and is now run by a number of renowned winemakers including Audrey Bonnet-Koenig, Claude Gros and Stéphane Canaguie.

Mas d’Amile.zin: Even so, Amélie d’Hurlaborde of Mas d’Amile says that the climate keeps reminding them to look after the indigenous varieties that have better resistance to drought, like Carignan.

Maxime Magnon.zin: After losing 50% of his crop in 2021, Maxime Magnon decided to buy vines in a completely different terroir, 20km away around Peyriac-de-Mer, ‘in order to diversify in terms of terroir, not to have everything so close together, ’ he says.
Maxime Magnon Originally from the Ain department in the east of France, Maxime Magnon has gained a solid reputation since launching the domaine in 2002.

Sarrat de Goundy.zin: Sarrat de Goundy Not only is the restaurant well worth a visit, but the wines are also very good, expressive and fine.

Terres Falmet.zin: Yves Falmet, of Domaine Terres Falmet in the south of the appellation, recalls that there was ‘strong mildew pressure’.

Thierry Navarre.zin: Thierry Navarre Based in the picturesque town of Roquebrun, Thierry Navarre followed in the footsteps of his grandfather and father, who were also ‘des hommes de la terre ’ (men of the earth), he says.

Cave Verdier-Logel.zin: Côtes du Forez Cave Verdier-Logel – the first serious independent producer here when the local cooperative was virtually the only producer in the area.
Cave Verdier-Logel has some of its vines here, on the steep slopes.

Château de Passavant.zin: Château de Passavant gets less media attention than some more high-profile Loire Chenin producers, so it is good to see its 2014 Jarret de Monchenin emerging as our only Outstanding wine.

Clos Rougeard.zin: Clos Rougeard’s history and terroir Copy by Yohan Castaing Clos Rougeard has always been a truly exceptional estate in the Saumur-Champigny appellation of the Loire.
Clos Rougeard’s Brezé white has become a cult wine, but another rarity is the Côteau de Saumur sweet wine, only produced in exceptional vintages such as 2018.

Didier Dagueneau.zin: After the untimely death of Didier Dagueneau in 2008, his son Louis-Benjamin has taken the domaine forward without losing sight of any of the principles of his father.
Another famous, and important, name is Domaine Didier Dagueneau, perhaps the most sought-after producer of groundbreaking Sancerre and Pouilly-Fumé wines.

Domaine Belargus.zin: Ivan Massonnat of Domaine Belargus in Anjou said: ‘From the end of March to the beginning of April, our team spent precisely 15 nights standing, fighting alongside our vines.
Domaine Belargus declares that 2023 was the rainiest harvest in the area for 10 years.

Domaine Brégeon.zin: Asked how he would describe Gorges wines, Fred Lailler clenches his fist: ‘They should be like gunflint.’ Lailler, winemaker and owner of Domaine Brégeon, explains that the wines are born from a subsoil of gabbro, a dense, dark and impenetrable igneous rock.

Domaine FL.zin: Regional France Domaine FL’s Savennières Roche-aux- Moines 2016 supports my conviction that if I could only drink a single style of wine for the rest of my life it would have to be Loire Chenin Blanc.

Domaine Grosbot-Barbara.zin: Domaine Grosbot-Barbara – Denis Barbara, the loose-limbed rock star of St-Pourçain, had the vision and determination to create the beautiful vineyard of Mont-Georges.

Domaine Huet.zin: Sarah Hwang, of Domaine Huet in Vouvray, reports a similarly long and complicated harvest, with 2023 taking twice as long as 2022.
Founded in the Loire village of Vouvray in 1928, Domaine Huet is revered for its ageworthy Chenin Blancs.

Domaine Ménard-Gaborit.zin: Yields were down 60% at Famille Lieubeau and 80% at Domaine Ménard-Gaborit – a bitter pill to swallow for 30-year-olds François Ménard and his wife Pauline, who took over the family domaine in 2021.

Domaine Ogereau.zin: He also exposes the dangers of drinks investment on his sites Investdrinks.org and Investdrinks-blog.blogspot.com Domaine Ogereau, L’Enthousiasme, Savennières 2014 I discovered this estate in 1990 when Vincent and Catherine were part of the new generation restoring Anjou.

Domaine Vacheron.zin: The terroir here is incredibly complex, and the best wines are finally getting the attention they deserve.’ Domaine Vacheron, a family winery that goes back four generations, was an early adopter of bottling terroir-specific wines.
Biodynamic producer Jean-Laurent Vacheron of Domaine Vacheron says, ‘We’ve never spent so much money for so little harvest.

Domaine Yannick Amirault.zin: These are the words of Benoît Amirault, of Domaine Yannick Amirault in Bourgueil.

Domaine de la Butte.zin: Winemaking The red grapes from Domaine de la Butte are totally destemmed, and both red and white grapes are thoroughly sorted on tables to ensure only the best grapes are used.

Domaine de la Pépière.zin: Since then, a number of leading producers – including Jo Landron, Vincent Caillé, Domaine Luneau-Papin and Domaine de la Pépière – have forged a distinct identity for their wines, and overall quality has increased immensely.

Domaine de la Taille aux Loups.zin: Jacky Blot (Domaine de la Taille aux Loups, Montlouis) is convinced that 2019 is a great vintage for white wines, and is much better than 2018.

Domaine des Bérioles.zin: Domaine des Bérioles – run by Jean Teissèdre, sister Sophie Roux and her husband Jérôme, this organic domaine is one of the best in the Upper Loire.

Domaine des Forges.zin: A top bottle to try is Domaine des Forges, Quarts de Chaume Grand Cru 2014 which has a rich and heady scent of grilled honeyed peaches, apricot and frangipane tart.

Domaine des Herbauges.zin: Loire white wine 2021: top producers At the time of tasing, many wines were yet to be bottled and released Claude Lafond Domaine Cady Domaine des Herbauges Famille Bourgeois Jean-François Mérieau Cross above the village of Chavignol with the town of Sancerre in the distance.

Domaine des Pothiers.zin: Domaine des Pothiers – now run by the dynamic Romain Paire who makes fine organic and biodynamic Côte Roannaise wines, including Riesling.

Domaine des Roches Neuves.zin: Thierry Germain, of Domaine des Roches Neuves in Saumur-Champigny, says the 2023 vintage has produced ‘the flesh of 2022, with the finesse of 2021 and fine tannins’.

Domaine des Sables Verts.zin: Hervé Malinge, of Domaine des Sables Verts in Saumur-Champigny, comments, ‘It was a very challenging vintage.

Domaine du Closel.zin: Evelyne de Pontbriand, owner of Domaine du Closel and president of the Savennières appellation, explains: ‘Until 10 years ago, we all harvested the grapes late, with botrytis – just like the sweet Chenins.

Domaine du Collier.zin: Growers such as Germain, Arnaud Lambert, Antoine Foucault (of Domaine du Collier) and Romain Guiberteau are producing consistently fine Chenins with the precision and chalky density that derive from these limestone-based soils.

François et Julien Pinon.zin: Julien Pinon, of François et Julien Pinon, says, ‘grey rot is a fungus, but acid rot is caused by a bacteria that turns wine into vinegar.

Frédéric Mabileau.zin: Seek out Frédéric Mabileau’s Chenin du Puy, Saumur 2016, which is lean and austere, but has a richness and ripeness to the fruit which brings balance.

Gilles Bonnefoy.zin: Gilles Bonnefoy in the Côtes du Forez has some vines at 600m, while Domaine Sérol (Côte Roannaise) has a parcel at 500m.

Grange Saint-Sauveur.zin: ‘People expect high-volume, standardised wine from Anjou,’ says winemaker Antoine Pouponneau of Grange Saint-Sauveur, who opts to produce his (excellent) Anjou wines under the humble Vin de France label.

Gérard Boulay.zin: Pristine wines Gérard Boulay is another famous producer, whose family have been cultivating wines in Chavignol since 1310.

Henri Bourgeois.zin: Much of the credit for putting Chavignol on the map must go to Henri Bourgeois, who was working with about 2ha in the 1950s, but it is a new generation that is pushing the boundaries further.
The 2020 Les Ruchons from Henri Bourgeois was one of Beverley Blanning MW’s favourites in her exploration of Sancerre’s revival.

Hubert Brochard.zin: I have little doubt that Hubert Brochard will continue to be a benchmark producer of white, red and rosé Sancerre for many years to come.
Hubert Brochard is one of the key family domaines, with a history dating back to 1900.

Jérémie Huchet.zin: This might be an extreme view, but certainly there are other winemakers, such as Jérémie Huchet, who are unconvinced that batonnage works for their terroir and style: ‘It erases the terroir,’ he says.

Mélaric.zin: Another top pick from Saumur is Mélaric, Billes de Roche, Saumur 2018, which is elegant and precise.

Paul Prieur & Fils.zin: Luc Prieur of Domaine Paul Prieur & Fils notes the ‘significant difference between those vineyards facing south and those which have a southeast or easterly exposition’.

Vincent Pinard.zin: The 2019 domaine Sancerre from Vincent Pinard shows that is possible to have ripe fruit, sufficient concentration as well as finesse and delicacy.

Blandy’s.zin: Buying over 50% of the island’s Malmsey grapes to produce Madeira’s sweetest style, the expertise of Blandy’s shines in the precision and balance of the 1981, the last remaining barrel of which was bottled in 2019 – producing just 999 bottles.
Blandy’s still has wines ageing in barrel and demi-john going back to the 1920 Bual.

Cossart Gordon.zin: Cossart Gordon dates back to 1745 and is the oldest company still trading on Madeira.

Beringer.zin: It also indicates that some larger wineries, like Beringer and J Lohr, are at an advantage in a tricky vintage as they can select the best fruit from their own vineyards and from those that supply them on a contract basis.

Black Stallion.zin: Black Stallion’s Gaspare Vineyard and Materra Cunate Family’s Vine 1 are densely packed wines; both will reward upfront and also age for up to 12 years.

Cardinale.zin: They have a lot of the same energy, expression and life’ explains Chris Carpenter, winemaker for Lokoya, Cardinale, La Jota and Mt Brave, all part of the large Jackson Family Wines portfolio.

Caterwaul.zin: Consider Caterwaul Cabernet Sauvignon, a $55 wine made by consultant winemaker Thomas Rivers Brown, also the mastermind behind $300+ Schrader wines.
